title: 3Sum
oneLinerQuestion: Find all unique triplets in an array that sum to zero.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The 3Sum problem asks us to find all unique triplets in an integer array that sum to zero. A brute-force search checking all combinations takes O(N^3) time and makes duplicate avoidance difficult. By sorting the array first, we can lock in one element at index 'i' and transform the remaining search into a classic Two-Pointer problem, reducing the overall time complexity to O(N^2) while easily skipping duplicates.

- Step 1: Array Sorting — We sort the input array in ascending order. Sorting enables monotonic pointer movement (increasing or decreasing the sum predictably) and groups duplicate values adjacent to each other so they can be skipped efficiently.

- Step 2: Outer Anchor Traversal — We iterate through the array using an index 'i' from 0 up to nums.length - 3. If nums[i] > 0, we can terminate early because three positive sorted numbers can never sum to zero. To ensure unique triplets, if i > 0 and nums[i] === nums[i - 1], we skip the current iteration.

- Step 3: Two-Pointer Search Initialization — For each fixed nums[i], we set two pointers: 'left = i + 1' and 'right = nums.length - 1'. The targeted sum for these two pointers is -nums[i] (meaning nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right] === 0).

- Step 4: Triplet Evaluation & Pointer Shifting — Inside a while loop (left < right), we compute currentSum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]. If currentSum < 0, we increment 'left++' to increase the sum. If currentSum > 0, we decrement 'right--' to decrease the sum.

- Step 5: Triplet Recording & Duplicate Bypassing — When currentSum === 0, we add [nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]] to our result set. To avoid duplicate triplets with the same anchor 'i', we advance 'left' past identical adjacent values (while left < right && nums[left] === nums[left + 1] left++) and decrement 'right' past identical adjacent values (while left < right && nums[right] === nums[right - 1] right--), then advance both pointers by one final step.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N^2) because sorting takes O(N log N) and the nested two-pointer traversal takes O(N) for each of the N elements. Space Complexity: O(1) or O(log N) auxiliary space depending on the sorting algorithm implementation, excluding the space required to store the output.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION threeSum(nums):
    SORT(nums), res = []
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 3 DO:
        IF i > 0 AND nums[i] == nums[i-1] THEN CONTINUE
        l = i + 1, r = LENGTH(nums) - 1
        WHILE l < r DO:
            sum = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
            IF sum == 0 THEN:
                APPEND [nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]] TO res
                WHILE l < r AND nums[l] == nums[l+1] DO l = l + 1
                WHILE l < r AND nums[r] == nums[r-1] DO r = r - 1
                l = l + 1, r = r - 1
            ELSE IF sum < 0 THEN l = l + 1
            ELSE r = r - 1
        END WHILE
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
